results.title: Troubleshooting Playback Audio Issues
results.summary: Focuses on dropouts and disconnections in live setups. Four checks: device/OS/app up to date, iOS performance (RAM, background apps), the USB connection (named as the most common cause in MultiOut setups), and the audio connection (Auto Pan splitter cable, class-compliant interfaces). The article does not cover no-sound, output selection, Bluetooth, sample rate, or mono/stereo settings.

steps.text: Check the device is supported (supported devices list for iOS, iPadOS, macOS). On the oldest supported iOS generation, Multi-Outs and MIDI Cue editing are limited.
Confirm the OS is up to date and that Playback support for it is confirmed (see the OS compatibility article). Update Playback from the iOS or Mac App Store.
steps.caution: Updating the app closes Playback and takes a few minutes; don't do this during a service.

steps.text: iOS performance: clear RAM, force-close all background apps before opening Playback, and do not multitask during a live performance.
USB adapter: an official Apple adapter is required (Lightning to USB3 or USB-C to USB3; both allow simultaneous charging).
USB cable length: max 16 feet for USB 2.0, 3 meters (9 feet) for USB 3.0. Keep the digital USB run short and use longer analog runs (XLR, 1/4") from the interface to DI boxes and the console.
Powered USB extension cables: base cable must respect the limits above; the active repeater needs external power; max extender length 25 m (USB 2.0) or 15 m (USB 3.0).
Powered USB hub: must be powered, no more than 7 USB accessory ports, and only one audio interface connected at a time so Playback sends audio to the correct device.
Auto Pan splitter cable: use a high-quality cable with as few adaptors as possible.
Audio interface: Playback is generally compatible with class-compliant USB interfaces; check the tested supported devices list on multitracks.com.
If issues persist, contact MultiTracks support.

results.title: HOW TO | Connect Playback to a Dante Network
results.summary: Playback can use a Dante network as its audio device over a single Ethernet cable instead of an interface and DI boxes. Two documented options. Option 1, Mac only: Dante Virtual Soundcard (DVS, up to 32 outputs, one-time license from Audinate), with the Mac on the Dante network by Cat-6 to a shared switch or router, using a USB-to-Ethernet adapter if the Mac has no Ethernet port; selected in Playback via Settings > General > Audio Device once DVS is running. Option 2, iOS and Mac: a Dante AVIO USB adapter (a USB dongle with an Ethernet port) limited to 2 outputs, output 1 click/guide and output 2 tracks; this is the ONLY documented way to put an iPad or iPhone on a Dante network. The article states Playback does NOT support Dante Via, and warns that not all USB Ethernet adapters work reliably, pointing to Audinate's adapter recommendations for macOS. SoundGrid is not covered here.

steps.text: Confirm the platform first: DVS is Mac only; an iPad or iPhone can only join a Dante network through a Dante AVIO USB adapter (2 outputs). A plain USB-to-Ethernet adapter on an iPad is not a documented Dante setup.
DVS (Mac): install Playback, then download Dante Virtual Soundcard and buy the one-time license from Audinate. Playback does not support Dante Via.
DVS (Mac): connect the Mac to the same wired network as the Dante devices with a Cat-6 cable to a shared switch or router. Dante needs a hard-wired connection, not Wi-Fi.

DVS (Mac): if the Mac has no built-in Ethernet port, use a USB-to-Ethernet adapter. The article warns not all adapters work reliably and links Audinate's FAQ 'DVS: USB Ethernet Adaptor Choice for macOS Systems' (https://www.audinate.com/learning/faqs/dvs-usb-ethernet-adaptor-choice-for-macos-systems), which recommends adapters that use the USB CDC-NCM driver standard and notes many common 1 Gbps adapters (Realtek RTL8153 chip) only support CDC-ECM.

DVS (Mac): in the DVS app choose the channel count (16x16 or 32x32 recommended), select the network interface the Dante network is on (a valid choice shows an IP address), then press Start. DVS must be running before it can appear as an audio device.

DVS (Mac): in Playback go to Settings > General, click the Audio Device cell, and choose Dante Virtual Soundcard. This also makes Dante the computer's audio device, so turn on Do Not Disturb to keep system sounds out of the track outputs.

DVS (Mac): route Playback buses to the outputs you want (the output count matches the DVS configuration, e.g. 16x16 gives 16), then patch Playback's outputs to destination devices in Dante Controller.

AVIO adapter (iOS and Mac): connect the Dante AVIO USB adapter between the device and the Dante network; it provides 2 outputs (output 1 click/guide, output 2 tracks). The article gives no further steps for this option. The supported-devices list marks the AVIO adapter as 'setup required'.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Live Performance > Tracks/Buses Mixer: Controlling Your Tracks
results.text:
Reference Track Fader and controls

- The reference track is muted by default.
- Soloing the reference track with the circle "S" button will solo the reference track and mute all tracks, including the click and guide.
- Tapping on the "reference" track name will unmute the reference track, and mute all instrument tracks, but keep the click and guide track with the reference.

Master Fader

Take full control of all audience-facing audio with the master track fader. This fader controls the overall volume output of all instrument tracks + buses, as well as the pad player.

Reminder: The master fader volume is globally set by default. For song specific master volume, enable this in General Settings.

- Tip: Do you need to perform a factory reset of Playback for any reason? Triple-Tap the master fader label to initiate a factory reset, wiping all downloaded data and logging out.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Playback Settings > Buses Settings Tab
results.text:
Bus Outputs

The Bus Settings tab is where Buses can be customized and outputs can be re-routed. Playback has 16 default buses with default SmartRouting that automatically route the related instrument tracks to each of the buses. However, Bus routing and naming is completely customizable and saved by audio device.

Quick Tip: Renaming Playback Buses in Bus Settings

- Swipe Left on any bus cell to Edit the name and abbreviation
- Name: Change the name of a Playback bus
- Abbreviation: Change the bus name shown under the fader in the Buses mixer
- Emojis are supported for bus names 😉

Note: For an in-depth overview of Playback bus routing and features, see:
​📖Bus Routing in Playback

Change Bus Routing

Bus Routing is saved and recalled based on the connected audio device and dependent on the number of supported outputs. If an audio interface has 10 outputs, then those 16 are available for routing.

- Tap the bus cell to open the routing menu
- Choose which output to route the bus to and press Done

Note: if a particular output is greyed-out, it's possible that the SMPTE bus is enabled and routed to that output. Either change the SMPTE output routing, or disable SMPTE output from the General Settings Tab if not intending to use it.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Playback Settings > Tracks Settings Tab
results.text:
Tracks Outputs

The Tracks Settings tab is where the default bus routing of every instrument part in the MultiTracks.com catalog can be adjusted. Scroll to any instrument part, Tap the row, and select the new bus that this track will be routed to.

Track routing in Playback is device specific, and is global for that track. So changing the routing for a track name "Electric guitar 3" will change that track's routing across all songs and setlists on that device.

results.title: How To | Track & Bus Routing in Playback
results.summary: Bus routing and MultiOuts require a Playback Premium subscription. Playback groups 150+ instruments into 16 buses plus a dedicated SMPTE bus; each bus can go to any available output on the selected audio device, mono or stereo. The Pad bus cannot be re-routed. Track routing is saved per device and applies globally to that track; it is not saved with setlists or named arrangements.

steps.text: Route tracks to buses: Settings > Tracks tab, assign each track to a bus (defaults are preset and can be overwritten).
Route buses to outputs: Settings > Buses tab, tap a bus row and choose an available output.
Route several buses at once: tap 'Assign Multiple Busses' in the bottom-right, select buses, assign one output.
Rename a bus: drag its row to the left to reveal Edit.
Greyed-out output: the SMPTE bus is probably using it. Disable SMPTE in the General tab or set the SMPTE bus to 'None'.

Alternative from the main interface: open the 'Busses' layer (bottom right next to the master fader, or cycle layers with the button beside it), tap Edit (top right) to enter Setlist/Song Map edit mode, tap a bus name and select the output.
Bus mixes are song-specific by default; disable Song Specific Buses in Settings for a global mix. Solo/mute on a bus affects all tracks routed to it.

results.title: HOW TO | Connect Playback to a Dante Network
results.summary: Playback can use a Dante network as its audio device over a single Ethernet cable instead of an interface and DI boxes. Two documented options. Option 1, Mac only: Dante Virtual Soundcard (DVS, up to 32 outputs, one-time license from Audinate), with the Mac on the Dante network by Cat-6 to a shared switch or router, using a USB-to-Ethernet adapter if the Mac has no Ethernet port; selected in Playback via Settings > General > Audio Device once DVS is running. Option 2, iOS and Mac: a Dante AVIO USB adapter (a USB dongle with an Ethernet port) limited to 2 outputs, output 1 click/guide and output 2 tracks; this is the ONLY documented way to put an iPad or iPhone on a Dante network. The article states Playback does NOT support Dante Via, and warns that not all USB Ethernet adapters work reliably, pointing to Audinate's adapter recommendations for macOS. SoundGrid is not covered here.

steps.text: Confirm the platform first: DVS is Mac only; an iPad or iPhone can only join a Dante network through a Dante AVIO USB adapter (2 outputs). A plain USB-to-Ethernet adapter on an iPad is not a documented Dante setup.
DVS (Mac): install Playback, then download Dante Virtual Soundcard and buy the one-time license from Audinate. Playback does not support Dante Via.
DVS (Mac): connect the Mac to the same wired network as the Dante devices with a Cat-6 cable to a shared switch or router. Dante needs a hard-wired connection, not Wi-Fi.

DVS (Mac): if the Mac has no built-in Ethernet port, use a USB-to-Ethernet adapter. The article warns not all adapters work reliably and links Audinate's FAQ 'DVS: USB Ethernet Adaptor Choice for macOS Systems' (https://www.audinate.com/learning/faqs/dvs-usb-ethernet-adaptor-choice-for-macos-systems), which recommends adapters that use the USB CDC-NCM driver standard and notes many common 1 Gbps adapters (Realtek RTL8153 chip) only support CDC-ECM.

DVS (Mac): in the DVS app choose the channel count (16x16 or 32x32 recommended), select the network interface the Dante network is on (a valid choice shows an IP address), then press Start. DVS must be running before it can appear as an audio device.

DVS (Mac): in Playback go to Settings > General, click the Audio Device cell, and choose Dante Virtual Soundcard. This also makes Dante the computer's audio device, so turn on Do Not Disturb to keep system sounds out of the track outputs.

DVS (Mac): route Playback buses to the outputs you want (the output count matches the DVS configuration, e.g. 16x16 gives 16), then patch Playback's outputs to destination devices in Dante Controller.

AVIO adapter (iOS and Mac): connect the Dante AVIO USB adapter between the device and the Dante network; it provides 2 outputs (output 1 click/guide, output 2 tracks). The article gives no further steps for this option. The supported-devices list marks the AVIO adapter as 'setup required'.

results.title: How to Use Playback with Your Sound System
results.summary: Three documented ways to get audio out of Playback: the built-in headphone port with Auto-Pan (2 channels: click/guide left, tracks right), a USB audio interface (up to 32 outputs, grouped into mono or stereo buses), and networked audio such as Dante or SoundGrid (iPad/iPhone limited to two channels; macOS can route up to 32 via Dante Virtual Soundcard). Bluetooth, subscription tiers, and menu paths are not covered here.

steps.text: Option 1 - headphone port: Auto-Pan is on by default. Use a 1/8" TRS to dual 1/4" TS cable, a stereo DI (or two mono DIs) to convert to XLR, then XLR to the stage box. Devices without a headphone jack can use a Lightning-to-3.5mm or USB-C-to-3.5mm adapter. Left channel feeds in-ears (click/guide); right feeds the house mix.

Option 2 - USB audio interface: up to 32 outputs via a supported class-compliant interface. Lightning devices need an Apple Lightning Digital AV Adapter; USB-C devices need an Apple USB-C Digital AV Multiport Adapter. Add a powered USB hub if the interface is bus-powered. Outputs are grouped into custom buses, mono or stereo.

Option 3 - networked audio (Dante, SoundGrid): connect the Playback device to a network running that protocol. iPad and iPhone support only two channels over networked audio; macOS apps like Dante Virtual Soundcard can route up to 32 channels.
Use an in-ear monitoring solution so click and guide are not heard by the congregation. Accompaniment tracks do not include click and guide.

results.title: Troubleshooting Playback Audio Issues
results.summary: Focuses on dropouts and disconnections in live setups. Four checks: device/OS/app up to date, iOS performance (RAM, background apps), the USB connection (named as the most common cause in MultiOut setups), and the audio connection (Auto Pan splitter cable, class-compliant interfaces). The article does not cover no-sound, output selection, Bluetooth, sample rate, or mono/stereo settings.

steps.text: Check the device is supported (supported devices list for iOS, iPadOS, macOS). On the oldest supported iOS generation, Multi-Outs and MIDI Cue editing are limited.
Confirm the OS is up to date and that Playback support for it is confirmed (see the OS compatibility article). Update Playback from the iOS or Mac App Store.
steps.caution: Updating the app closes Playback and takes a few minutes; don't do this during a service.

steps.text: iOS performance: clear RAM, force-close all background apps before opening Playback, and do not multitask during a live performance.
USB adapter: an official Apple adapter is required (Lightning to USB3 or USB-C to USB3; both allow simultaneous charging).
USB cable length: max 16 feet for USB 2.0, 3 meters (9 feet) for USB 3.0. Keep the digital USB run short and use longer analog runs (XLR, 1/4") from the interface to DI boxes and the console.
Powered USB extension cables: base cable must respect the limits above; the active repeater needs external power; max extender length 25 m (USB 2.0) or 15 m (USB 3.0).
Powered USB hub: must be powered, no more than 7 USB accessory ports, and only one audio interface connected at a time so Playback sends audio to the correct device.
Auto Pan splitter cable: use a high-quality cable with as few adaptors as possible.
Audio interface: Playback is generally compatible with class-compliant USB interfaces; check the tested supported devices list on multitracks.com.
If issues persist, contact MultiTracks support.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Playback Settings > Side Menu: Settings & Features
results.text:
Playback's side menu has the following features:

- Main Settings Menu
- Waveform Size: adjustment
- Notifications: To toggle in-app notifications on or off.
- Playback Sync: To enable or disable Playback Sync broadcast from the Playback device.
- Playback Remote: The main Playback Remote menu to initiate a Playback Remote session, and/or connect a remote Playback device to a host Playback device. (📖Learn More)
- Network: the area to select which specific IP Address or network Playback Sync and Playback Remote broadcast through on host devices. (When utilizing multiple IP addresses or networks on a MacOS device).
- User Name, Organization Name, and Organization ID Number.
- Switch Organizations to switch between available organizations the signed-in user has access to.
- Log Out to log out the currently signed-in user of Playback.

Opening "Settings" in Playback's side menu will reveal the main Settings menu with the five settings' tabs; General, Tacks, Buses, MIDI, and About.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Playback Settings > Buses Settings Tab
results.text:
Bus Outputs

The Bus Settings tab is where Buses can be customized and outputs can be re-routed. Playback has 16 default buses with default SmartRouting that automatically route the related instrument tracks to each of the buses. However, Bus routing and naming is completely customizable and saved by audio device.

Quick Tip: Renaming Playback Buses in Bus Settings

- Swipe Left on any bus cell to Edit the name and abbreviation
- Name: Change the name of a Playback bus
- Abbreviation: Change the bus name shown under the fader in the Buses mixer
- Emojis are supported for bus names 😉

Note: For an in-depth overview of Playback bus routing and features, see:
​📖Bus Routing in Playback

Change Bus Routing

Bus Routing is saved and recalled based on the connected audio device and dependent on the number of supported outputs. If an audio interface has 10 outputs, then those 16 are available for routing.

- Tap the bus cell to open the routing menu
- Choose which output to route the bus to and press Done

Note: if a particular output is greyed-out, it's possible that the SMPTE bus is enabled and routed to that output. Either change the SMPTE output routing, or disable SMPTE output from the General Settings Tab if not intending to use it.
